lines: A stereo processor that records into a rolling buffer and mangles the clock division that has gone past, with tape failures, digital breakage and media corruption
Note — The wet path always plays the division before the one being recorded, so it lags the input by one division; above the bottom tenth of MIX the dry side is delayed to match
Note — Rack does not save audio in a patch, so a freshly loaded module passes the incoming audio through until it has captured one whole TIME window, then crossfades into the saved MIX setting
Note — DAMAGE and CV AMT are each one knob over three stored channels, Bend, Break and Corrupt. The square button beside each cycles the channel, and the knob snaps to that channel's stored value
Note — A damage channel that does nothing in the current mode dims to a quarter brightness on the panel
Note — In Macro mode the module rolls fresh Bend and Break manipulations every division
Note — In Micro mode you drive it by hand: the micro speed knob sets the playback rate, the bend gate flips reverse, and the break channel becomes traverse or silence
Note — The checksum artwork is driven by the audio: cyan displacement from Bend, amber broken rows from Break, red-orange blocks from Corrupt, with a readout of the division and corrupt effect
Sets the period captured and played: on the internal clock, from 16 seconds down to 80Hz; on the external clock, one of nine divisions and multiples of the clock input, a sixteenth to eight times
Subdivides each division into whole stutter repeats, from 1 up to 1024; the curve keeps the rhythmic counts in the lower half of the travel and audio rate at the top
Fades between dry and wet, fully dry at the bottom of its travel and the captured division alone at the top; through the bottom tenth the dry side shifts from the incoming audio to that division
Sets the amount of the damage channel the square button beside it has selected, each of the three holding its own value
Attenuates the CV jack of the damage channel the square button beside it has selected: fully anticlockwise blocks the CV and fully clockwise passes it at full depth, with no inversion
Sets the manual playback speed over a range of three octaves each way; it applies in Micro mode, and in Macro mode as well when the menu turns it on there
Cycles the damage knob between the Bend, Break and Corrupt channels
Cycles the CV attenuator between the Bend, Break and Corrupt channels
Switches between Macro, where the module rolls its own manipulations each division, and Micro, where the speed knob and the gates drive playback by hand
Switches the clock between the module's own and the clock input jack
Holds the audio memory so the same block keeps playing; it engages on the next division, and by default each press latches
The left audio input, which also feeds the right channel when the right jack has nothing patched
The right audio input
Added to the TIME knob, a tenth of a turn per volt, with the total held inside the knob's travel
Added to the REPEAT knob, a tenth of a turn per volt, with the total held inside the knob's travel
Added to the MIX knob, a tenth of a turn per volt, with the total held inside the knob's travel
Added to the Bend channel's stored amount through the Bend CV attenuator, a tenth of a turn per volt; in Micro mode it also sets the playback pitch at 1V per octave
Added to the Break channel's stored amount through the Break CV attenuator, a tenth of a turn per volt, with the total held inside the knob's travel
Added to the Corrupt channel's stored amount through the Corrupt CV attenuator, a tenth of a turn per volt; 0V or less while it is patched turns Corrupt off altogether
In Macro mode a rising edge above 0.4V switches Bend on or off; in Micro mode it switches reverse playback on or off
In Macro mode a rising edge above 0.4V switches Break on or off; in Micro mode it switches between traverse and silence
A rising edge above 0.4V steps to the next corrupt effect
A rising edge above 0.4V switches Freeze on or off, taking effect at the next division
The clock read when the clock source is set to external; the TIME knob then divides or multiplies the edges arriving here
A rising edge above 0.4V restarts the internal clock at once, or, on an external clock, realigns the division count at the next edge
The left side of the processed stereo output, at line level
The right side of the processed stereo output, at line level
Menu — Corrupt effect: Decimate, Dropout, Destroy, DJ Filter, Vinyl Sim — picks which media damage the Corrupt channel applies
Menu — Limit Corrupt to original 3 effects — leaves only Decimate, Dropout and Destroy in the list the corrupt gate steps through
Menu — Macro: Bend enabled — switches the Bend channel on or off in Macro mode
Menu — Macro: Break enabled — switches the Break channel on or off in Macro mode
Menu — Micro: reverse playback — plays the captured division backwards in Micro mode
Menu — Micro: Break knob = silence (off = traverse) — chooses whether the Break channel's knob sets a silent duty cycle or selects which subsection of the division loops
Menu — MICRO knob active in Macro (global varispeed) — lets the micro speed knob change the playback rate in Macro mode as well
Menu — Stereo: unique per channel — rolls the Bend and Break manipulations separately for the left and right channels
Menu — Gates: momentary (hold) instead of latching — makes the four gate jacks act only while they are held high, rather than toggling on each rising edge
Menu — Freeze button: momentary — makes the freeze button hold only while it is pressed
Menu — Glitch windowing — sets the fade applied at slice edges, trading hard clicks against softened transients
Menu — Stereo width — narrows the wet buffer, fully anticlockwise collapsing it to mono and fully clockwise keeping the original left and right image
Menu — LED brightness — sets how brightly the panel lamps are lit
Menu — Clear buffer — empties the recorded audio and starts the capture again
Menu — Restore default settings — puts every menu setting back to its default

BadSector.notes: Index order is not panel order in the gate row: the freeze gate is input 11 but is the leftmost jack of that row, with bend, break and corrupt to its right as inputs 8, 9 and 10. The three menu sliders (Glitch windowing, Stereo width, LED brightness) are ui::Slider widgets rather than params, so they cannot be clicked on the panel. The knob's damage and CV channels are stored per channel and swapped by the square buttons, so one param index covers three different settings depending on which channel is selected. configBypass wires the left and right inputs straight to the matching outputs.

lines: Three random control voltages that change together on a clock, each with its own depth and its own centre
Note — With nothing patched into the clock jack the module runs on its own clock, at a rate chosen in the menu
Note — Each output's centre is shifted by an offset chosen in the menu, and the result is held between -10V and +10V
Note — It is an adaptation of the open-source HAGIWO MOD1 hardware, whose jack wiring fixes F1 as the only input and F2, F3 and F4 as the three outputs
Chooses whether the outputs glide from one random value to the next across the gap between clocks, or jump straight to it and hold
Sets how far the first random voltage swings either side of its centre, from nothing at the bottom to 5V at the top
Sets how far the second random voltage swings either side of its centre, from nothing at the bottom to 5V at the top
Sets how far the third random voltage swings either side of its centre, from nothing at the bottom to 5V at the top
Draws a fresh set of random values at once, without waiting for a clock
A rising edge above 1V draws a fresh set of random values; the measured time between edges also sets how long the smooth glide takes
The first random voltage, its swing set by POT1 and its centre by the menu offset
The second random voltage, its swing set by POT2 and its centre by the menu offset
The third random voltage, its swing set by POT3 and its centre by the menu offset
Menu — Clock rate — sets the module's own clock rate, used only while the clock jack is unpatched, from 0.1Hz up to 3Hz
Menu — CV1 offset — shifts the first output's centre, from -5V to +5V
Menu — CV2 offset — shifts the second output's centre, from -5V to +5V
Menu — CV3 offset — shifts the third output's centre, from -5V to +5V
MOD1-RandomCV.notes: The panel prints POT1, POT2 and POT3 over the three knobs, S&H beside the switch, and CLK with F1 in over the input jack against CV1, CV2 and CV3 with F2, F3 and F4 over the outputs; the maker's tooltips use the F numbers. The button and the lamp under it carry no printed label. With a knob at full and the offset at zero the swing is 5V either way, and the menu offset can push the total to the -10V and +10V clamp.

lines: A sixteen voice generative synthesiser whose two streams, Pulsar and Quasar, each feed their own last pitch and note length into the next ones
Note — With no Quasar output patched, both eight voice banks are summed into Pulsar and the polyphony knob reaches sixteen; patching any Quasar jack splits the streams and caps the knob at eight
Note — Turn the polyphony knob to zero and patch a clock to the poly jack, and the module steps on that clock instead of its own timing, with the coupling knob choosing the division
Note — The menu loads a WAV file of 256-sample frames as a custom wavetable, and a scale.txt as custom scales; both paths are stored with the patch and the defaults can be restored from the same menu
Note — The menu can send the notes out as MIDI, Pulsar on channel 1 and Quasar on channel 2, once a driver and device are chosen
Sets how many voices are sounding, up to eight per stream, or sixteen on Pulsar alone when no Quasar output is patched; at zero with a clock in the poly jack the module runs in sync mode
Transposes everything, two octaves down at the bottom of its travel and two octaves up at the top
Chooses one of sixteen built-in scales, or one of the scales from a loaded scale file, that the generated pitches are drawn from
Sets how long a voice takes to slide to its new pitch, as a fraction of that note's own length, so short notes glide proportionally faster
Sets how wide a pitch range the generator draws from, the root alone at the bottom of its travel and about six octaves at the top
Sets the note length, sweeping from audio-rate grains at the bottom of its travel to notes tens of seconds long at the top; in sync mode it chooses the clock division instead
Morphs through the eight frames of the selected wavetable preset
Moves the peak of each note's envelope, a sharp attack with a long decay at one end and a slow swell at the other
Starts a fresh trajectory for the Pulsar voices
Starts a fresh trajectory for the Quasar voices
Holds the generator on its current pitches instead of stepping them on, while note lengths and envelopes carry on
Transposes everything at 1V per octave, added to the root knob
Adds to the polyphony knob, about one voice for every 1.25V; with the knob at zero it is read as a clock instead and the module steps on its rising edges
Added to the glide knob, a tenth of its travel per volt, with the total held inside that travel
Added to the spread knob, a tenth of its travel per volt, with the total held inside that travel
Added to the wave knob, a tenth of its travel per volt, with the total held inside that travel
Added to the envelope knob, a tenth of its travel per volt, with the total held inside that travel
Added to the coupling knob, a tenth of its travel per volt, with the total held inside that travel
1V or more holds the generator on its current pitches, while note lengths and envelopes carry on
1V or more starts a fresh trajectory for the Pulsar voices
1V or more starts a fresh trajectory for the Quasar voices
The Pulsar stream's audio, soft-clipped to roughly ±5V; with no Quasar output patched it carries both voice banks
The Quasar stream's audio, soft-clipped to roughly ±5V; it is silent while no Quasar output is patched
The pitch of the first Pulsar voice at 1V per octave, dropping to 0V while that voice is idle
10V while the first Pulsar voice is inside the gate length set in the menu, and 0V otherwise
The pitch of the first Quasar voice at 1V per octave, dropping to 0V while that voice is idle
10V while the first Quasar voice is inside the gate length set in the menu, and 0V otherwise
Menu — Load wavetable (.wav, 256-sample frames)... — reads a mono or multichannel WAV as custom wavetable frames
Menu — Restore default wavetable — drops a loaded wavetable and goes back to the 64 built-in frames
Menu — Load scales (scale.txt)... — reads a scale file in place of the sixteen built-in scales
Menu — Restore default scales — drops a loaded scale file and goes back to the built-in scales
Menu — Driver — chooses which MIDI system the note output is sent through
Menu — Device — chooses which MIDI port the note output is sent to
Menu — Monophonic (1 voice per channel) — sends one note at a time on each MIDI channel instead of the whole stream
Menu — Gate length — sets what fraction of each note the gate outputs and the MIDI notes stay on for, from 20% to 95%
Menu — Wavetable preset — chooses which block of eight frames the wave knob morphs through
Menu — Filter type: Off, Low-pass, Band-pass, High-pass — puts a state variable filter on every voice
Menu — Filter cutoff — sets the filter's corner, sweeping from 20Hz at the lowest setting to about 18kHz at the highest
Menu — Filter resonance — sets the filter's Q, from 0.5 at the lowest setting to 10 at the highest
Menu — Wavetable index — shifts the whole wavetable selection on by a fixed number of frames
Menu — Note length — scales every generated note length, a quarter of it at the shortest setting and four times at the longest

Entwine.notes: Despite the name and the sixteen voices, every output is mono: the pitch and gate jacks report voice zero of their stream only (src/Entwine.cpp:611-616), and the audio jacks carry the summed voices on one channel. The scales are stored as offset tables with no names (src/EntwineData.hpp:80), so no scale can be named in a line. The lock and reseed jacks are read as levels of 1V or more rather than through a Schmitt trigger, so a slow ramp will retrigger them. The polyphony knob's top value changes between 8 and 16 as Quasar outputs are patched and unpatched.

lines: A four channel event memory that learns which of its trigger inputs tend to follow one another, and how fast, then generates new trigger patterns from what it learned
Note — Learning is on from the moment the module is added: patch related triggers into A to D and the constellation builds on the display before anything is generated
Note — At the bottom of the MORPH knob's travel the four inputs pass straight through; turning it towards DREAM replaces more and more of the incoming events with ones chosen from the learned model
Note — With every event input and the clock jack unpatched, a learned constellation free-runs at the pace it was recorded at, and the density knob stretches or compresses that pace
Note — The display is the real transition table: a coloured line means one event has been observed following another, and its brightness and thickness show how likely that is
Sets how many previous events are used as the context for the next choice, from one to four; a longer context keeps recognisable phrases and a shorter one wanders more
Sharpens the learned preferences: low settings flatten the choices towards even odds, high settings strongly favour the paths already seen
Blends the learned choices towards the ones never taken, so unexplored transitions start to appear
Sets how likely a generated event is on each clock edge, and how fast a free-running constellation moves
Moves from passing the four inputs through unaltered at the bottom of its travel to replacing them with learned choices at the DREAM end
Switches learning on and off, leaving what has already been learned in place
Freezes the learned constellation so it stops being updated, without changing the learn setting
Attenuates and inverts the morph CV, -1 to +1, before it is added to the MORPH knob; at full positive, 0 to 10V covers the knob's whole travel
A rising edge above 1V is an event on that channel: it is learned, and it is either passed through or replaced by a learned choice according to MORPH
A rising edge above 1V calls for a generated event, whose likelihood comes from MORPH and the density knob
A rising edge above 1V returns the playback context to the phrase most recently learned, without deleting anything
Added to the MORPH knob through the attenuverter beside it, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, with the total held inside that travel
A 10V trigger whenever that channel fires, whether it was passed through or generated; its length is set in the menu
A voltage from 0V to 10V showing how well learned the most recent generated choice was, sliding smoothly to each new value; a passed-through or uncertain event reads low
Menu — Clear learned constellation — throws away everything learned and starts again empty
Menu — Reseed dream generator — restarts the random generator that picks between learned choices
Menu — Trigger length — sets how long the event output pulses last, from 1ms to 20ms

Constellate.notes: The four event inputs behave identically and share one line, as do the four event outputs; the display node colours are what tells them apart. Learning keeps a separate history from playback, so generated choices are never fed back into the model. The clock input only produces events while MORPH is above LIVE, because the event probability is MORPH multiplied by a density term (src/Constellate.cpp:350).
